verdicts.reviewer_notes: Sixth review, done independently of earlier review files. I re-fetched both cited URLs on 2026-10-08. SOURCE 1, the signed order PDF (gov.ca.gov FINAL-N-9-26-AI-EO-9.18.26-SIGNED.pdf): I read all 3 pages in full. Header 'EXECUTIVE ORDER N-9-26'. It is issued 'to become effective immediately' and signed and sealed 'this 18th day of September 2026', so event_date 2026-09-18 and stage in_force are correct. Para 1: 'No later than May 1, 2027, the Government Operations Agency shall complete the requirements of Section 8898.1 of the Government Code and develop application requirements, procedures, and criteria for independent verification organizations and publicly post them, as required by law.' The summary matches. Para 2: 'No later than December 1, 2027 ... complete the requirements of subdivision (a) of Section 11549.82 ... and begin taking the actions required by subdivision (b)'. The summary matches. Para 3: 'The Government Operations Agency, in consultation with the Governor's Office of Emergency Services, shall, no later than November 16, 2026, submit to my office recommendations, developed in consultation with national experts, addressing the technical feasibility and potential efficacy of amendments to existing state laws regarding AI safety and security, including at least' sub-items a to d. The summary gets who submits right (GovOps alone, in consultation with Cal OES), to whom (the Governor's office), when (16 Nov 2026), the national-experts consultation and the feasibility/efficacy framing. Sub-items: (a) embedding designated IVOs onsite at all large frontier developers, (b) independent verification of the safety frameworks, transparency reports and risk assessments that companies must file, (c) a kill switch whose efficacy an IVO verifies on an ongoing basis, (d) a critical-safety-incident definition updated to include a range of loss-of-control incidents. The summary's four topics match. The no-enforceable-rights sentence matches the order's closing clause. 'Its directives are addressed to state agencies' is a fair reading: every ordered paragraph is addressed to GovOps, plus the Secretary of State filing direction. TITLE: 'sets deadlines for independent verification rules' is accurate for paras 1 and 2. 'seeks recommendations on a frontier-model kill switch and loss-of-control incident reporting' correctly presents the kill switch and incident items as recommendation topics only, not requirements. Item (d) concerns the incidents companies 'are required to report', so 'incident reporting' is accurate. WHY_IT_MATTERS: 'does not change obligations for frontier developers today' is supported: the order binds only GovOps, creates no enforceable rights, and asks only for feasibility/efficacy recommendations on amendments. 'Signals the content of possible amendments to California's existing AI safety and security laws' is consistent with the order's text and with its final WHEREAS ('develop a roadmap for further strengthening our nation-leading laws'). The 16 Nov 2026 date is correct. SOURCE 2, the 23 Sept 2026 gov.ca.gov release: it refers to 'his recent AI executive order' without giving the number or date. It says the order directs GovOps to accelerate SB 813 / AB 1405 implementation and convene national experts, and it uses the 'advance the creation of a kill switch' wording. The item uses that wording neither in its title nor in its summary, so the release's framing does not leak in. TIER: both URLs are the Governor's office, the issuing body, so primary is correct. Confidence high fits: the primary text was read in full and its date and status match. DUPLICATES: no file in content/items/ mentions N-9-26 or a kill switch (grep). The nearest item, us-ca-sb-813-ab-1405-ai-third-party-verification (event_date 2026-09-09), covers the separate bill signing. instrument_slug resolves to the instrument candidate and to content/instruments/us-ca-eo-n-9-26-frontier-ai-oversight.json. TONE: neutral. The order's own partisan language (a 'failure of leadership by the President and Congressional leaders') is not repeated. Type 'regulation' is the nearest ITEM_TYPES value, since there is no executive-order type. MINOR, NOT BLOCKING (optional polish): (1) The summary's 'a kill switch for frontier models verified by an independent verification organization' compresses the order's 'with the efficacy of the switch verified on an ongoing basis by an independent verification organization'. 'whose efficacy is verified on an ongoing basis by an independent verification organization' would be more exact. (2) why_it_matters' 'deadlines ... to implement Gov. Code 8898.1 and 11549.82' is shorthand. For 11549.82 the deadline is to complete subdivision (a) and only begin (b). The summary states this precisely, so the shorthand does not mislead.
